title: The Concept of the Looking-Glass Self
text:
This concept, introduced by George Herbert Mead and later elaborated by Charles Horton Cooley, suggests that an individual's sense of self is derived from the perceived judgments of others. It posits that people view themselves through the imagined eyes of their community or social circle.

The looking-glass metaphor implies a continuous process where one anticipates how others perceive them—how they are judged, evaluated, and reflected back to them. This feedback mechanism shapes the internal sense of identity far more than purely objective self-reflection.

Understanding this dynamic is crucial for analyzing group behavior, social conformity, and the development of moral consciousness within a given cultural framework.
